messages:
Liam: heads-up: ran through the mac quickstart and got tripped by keychain behavior. the installer enabled the OS keychain credential helper by default, but our sample-app docs still show mounting ~/.redwood into containers. tokens saved to macOS Keychain are not available inside Docker which confused everyone.

Ari: can you paste repro? I thought keychain was supposed to be recommended on mac.

Liam: steps:
1) fresh mac, homebrew install redwoodctl (installer enables keychain helper)
2) `redwoodctl login --profile dev` -> token stored in Keychain (no file in ~/.redwood/tokens)
3) follow sample-app quickstart and run container mounting host ~/.redwood into /root/.redwood in container
4) inside container `redwoodctl status` -> unauthenticated, CLI complains `no token files found`

Liam: folks assume mounting ~/.redwood is the right way to share credentials, but on mac the tokens are in the keychain and don't show up. then they try headless login in container and create duplicated file-based tokens, leading to confusion about which credential is used by which environment.

Maria: ohhh. i saw this too. new hires run quickstart, see CLI working on host, then run the docker sample and it asks them to login. they do headless in container and accidentally generate project CI tokens on their laptop. not ideal.

Ari: two problems: 1) installer default opts into keychain without calling out container/device portability tradeoffs, 2) quickstart docs still recommend mounting ~/.redwood. both need fixes.

Liam: short-term workarounds i used: 1) explicitly set `REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE=file` before quickstart so tokens are file-backed and visible to containers, or 2) set REDWOOD_HOME to a per-project dir and mount that directory into container instead of host home.

Maria: implementation proposals:
- make installer prompt: "Store tokens in OS keychain (recommended for interactive desktops) or in files (better for containers/CI)? [keychain/file]" with recommended defaults based on detected environment (TTY + OS).
- add `redwoodctl login --store=file|keychain` and `REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE` env var so quickstart examples can force file store in sample apps/CI
- docs: update quickstart to never show mounting $HOME/.redwood; show `-e REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE=file -v $(pwd)/.redwood:/root/.redwood` example instead
- doctor: `redwoodctl doctor` should detect when tokens are stored in keychain and warn if sample-apps may mount ~/.redwood; also show a migration helper `redwoodctl tokens export --to file --path ./ci/redwood`

Ari: CLI changes sound good. also add behavior so that when REDWOOD_HOME is mounted from a container or when running with `--headless` we default to file store even if the system default is keychain (unless explicitly overridden). that avoids surprising headless flows creating keychain entries that are inaccessible.

Liam: edge case: people who have both keychain tokens and file tokens. we should have clear precedence rules and a visible `redwoodctl tokens list --all` that shows both stores with paths/hints. right now it's confusing which store wins.

Maria: tests we need: unit tests for store selection precedence, integration test on mac runner verifying file vs keychain behavior, and an e2e sample-app run showing container access when REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE=file is set.

Ari: ops note: update the sample CI images to set `REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE=file` and add a small onboarding blurb: "If you use macOS Keychain for interactive usage, set REDWOOD_TOKEN_STORE=file for CI or containerized runs."

devex-bot: created issue #4214: "redwoodctl: clarify and control token store (keychain vs file); avoid token invisibility in containers" and assigned to @ari for triage :spiral_note_pad:

ci-bot: scheduled CI job `devex/token-store-matrix` to run against ari/token-store-cli branch

Liam: thanks. can we also add an FAQ entry near install that explains: macOS Keychain tokens are not exported to Linux containers; use file store for portability, or explicitly export tokens for CI with `redwoodctl tokens export`? new hires hit this frequently.

Maria: will update quickstart + onboarding checklist once PR lands. thanks for reporting, @liam :thumbsup:
